services.description: Certify an opentine .tine artifact (format v2) BEFORE you pay for the work product it describes: re-derive every content-addressed step hash, check the parent chain, reject duplicate/replayed and dangling-referenced steps, and return an HMAC-SHA256 signed certification (certified | rejected + machine-readable reasons). States provenance facts only -- structural validity of the run history, never the quality of the work. Zero custody: DDG stores digests and verdicts, never artifact bodies, and never executes the artifact.

operation.description: Body {tine_b64 <= 512KB decoded} or {tine}. Runs the four .tine v2 checks in order (format, step_hashes, chain, completeness); a certified verdict requires all four, any failure is rejected fail closed with reasons[] (step_hash_mismatch@i, duplicate_step_hash@i, chain_link_mismatch@i, chain_root_link_invalid@0, chain_sequence_mismatch, chain_root_hash_mismatch, parent_ref_malformed, parent_step_index_invalid, parent_step_index_out_of_range, dangling_step_ref@i, step_index_mismatch@i, run_id_invalid, artifact_not_json, artifact_not_object, ...). Returns {certification_id:'crt_<16hex>', result:'certified'|'rejected', reason, reasons[], checks:[{name:'format'|'step_hashes'|'chain'|'completeness', pass, detail}], artifact_sha256 (canonical content digest), body_sha256 (exact submitted bytes), steps_verified, issued_at, key_id, sig, statement, cached:false, disclaimer}. Re-certifying the identical artifact inside DDG_CERTIFY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 24h) returns the stored certification with cached:true and re-signs nothing. Body {tine_hash} (64 hex) reads back a stored certification by digest, 404 when the digest was never certified. Result is a signed fact about provenance, not a judgement about the work.

200.description: Signed certification statement: result certified|rejected, the four checks, reasons[] ([] when certified), artifact_sha256, body_sha256, certification_id, issued_at, key_id, sig. A cached:true body is the stored certification re-read (no re-sign).

400.description: missing_artifact (neither tine_b64 nor tine_hash), invalid_base64, tine_hash_invalid.

402.description: Edge x402 challenge (the route is paid at $0.02; a paid tier route is dispatched after the payment gate).

404.description: artifact_not_certified (tine_hash not in the registry; bodies are never stored, certify with tine_b64 first).

413.description: artifact_too_large (decoded artifact above DDG_CERTIFY_MAX_BYTES, hard ceiling 512KB).

operation.summary: Certify an uploaded .tine v2 artifact ($0.02) or read a stored certification by tine_hash.

services.description: Free read of a certification: look a stored certification up by cert_id and re-verify it against its HMAC-SHA256 signature (a tampered registry row reads valid:false), or independently re-verify a {statement, sig} pair a buyer was handed, anywhere, with no DDG state involved. Fail closed on tamper: any mutated field or flipped signature byte makes the pair invalid. Free ($0) per spec; the single edge price floor knob is DDG_CERTIFY_FREE_ROUTE_PRICE (flip to "0.001" only if the edge 402s a zero-amount route).

operation.description: Body {cert_id} (alias certification_id) OR {statement, sig}. By cert_id: reads the stored row and re-verifies the statement against its signature, returning {ok, valid, checks_pass, issued_at, certification_id, result, artifact_sha256, reasons[], key_id, source:'registry', disclaimer}. By statement+sig: recomputes the HMAC over the canonical statement -- a mutated field (result, artifact_sha256, issued_at, steps_verified, key_id, ...) or a flipped sig nibble returns valid:false rather than an error. A stored rejection is a signed fact too: valid:true with result 'rejected' and checks_pass:false. Never writes, never moves funds.

200.description: The re-verified certification: valid, checks_pass, issued_at, certification_id, result, artifact_sha256, reasons[]. valid:false is the fail-closed answer for a tampered statement or row.

400.description: cert_id_or_statement_required, invalid_statement ('statement' is not an object), missing_sig.

operation.summary: Verify a stored certification by id, or any {statement, sig} pair independently (free).

services.description: Buyer-side certification: the sub-agent says its work product is at https://... -- fetch that .tine artifact (SSRF-guarded: https only, ports 443/8443, private/reserved/loopback blocked, resolve-then-connect pinning; 10s timeout; 512KB cap), run the full four-check certification and optionally compare expect_sha256 against the canonical content digest or the exact-body digest. Returns a signed certification carrying source_url, so the buyer pays only for output whose provenance chain actually verifies. An expectation mismatch is a request-level rejection (expect_sha256_mismatch) that issues no certificate and never touches the artifact's registry entry. Zero custody: bodies are fetched, digested and dropped, never stored.

operation.description: Body {url (https), expect_sha256? (64 hex)}. Fetches the artifact with the e10 SSRF guard and the pinned opener, certifies the fetched bytes and returns the same signed certification body as /v1/certify/run plus {source_url, upstream_status, fetched_bytes, expect_sha256_matched: true|false|null, service:'certify_verify_remote'}; a 512KB+ body is refused before hashing. expect_sha256 matches either artifact_sha256 (canonical content digest) or body_sha256 (exact bytes); a mismatch returns result:'rejected' with reasons[] containing expect_sha256_mismatch, expect_sha256_matched:false and no certification_id/sig (nothing new is attested about the artifact). Re-certifying an artifact already in the registry inside the cache TTL returns the stored certification with cached:true.

200.description: Signed certification of the fetched artifact: result certified|rejected, checks[4], reasons[], artifact_sha256, body_sha256, certification_id, issued_at, key_id, sig, source_url, upstream_status, fetched_bytes, expect_sha256_matched, cached.
